Subject: Alignment: Flagship Launch readiness — cross-functional owners and final asks

Team — pulling this thread together as we head into the final QBR review on Wednesday. High level ask: we need a single-page readiness snapshot from each owner by EOD Monday so leadership can roll up a deterministic go/no-go recommendation. Please include owner commitments for any high-risk open items, expected mitigation by date, and whether an SLA exception is required.

Quick checklist for each function (please use these headings in your one-pager):
- GTM / Sales: coverage for top 25 accounts, final demo script, pricing sheet alignment
- Enablement: all playbooks published, trainer schedule, pick-two customer-facing collateral pieces
- Pricing / Finance: approved list price, approved discount bands and escalation path
- Docs / DevRel: runbook link, two quickstart templates, API changelog signoff
- Support / CS: Tier 1 runbook, escalation matrix, on-call ramp plan for first 30 days

Specific asks by owner:
- Marissa: confirm enablement playbook status and attach the trainer calendar.
- Marcus: verify runtime SLA for 99th p95 latency guarantees and flag fallback model for degraded capacity.
- Laura: confirm named account coverage and any pre-approved promo for initial customers.
- Aditya: please finalize the QBR slide (metrics + risks) and paste the link to the HubSpot deal.
- Vivek: confirm support staffing model for the week after launch; include pager rotations and escalation points.

I attached the latest runbook and a template to populate. Short and specific — leadership wants one slide per function. If you absolutely cannot hit EOD Monday, flag a firm time when you can deliver.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor

Thanks — quick technical note (flagging for SLA and contingency planning): our current runtime benchmarking shows we can meet the customer-level p95 latency target at planned loads for the first 30 days, but only when the CPU/GPU mix is at the committed Dedicated pool configuration. Two items to decide:
1) Fallback model: if Dedicated capacity is constrained we can automatically route to a lower-capacity quantized model with a small quality delta. That requires a feature flag and a documented customer-facing note (Marketing + Docs) and an explicit SLA exception for quality variance.
2) Cache priming: to guarantee p95 under peak crest, we recommend a short warm-up window (30–45 minutes) after any large model rollback or code push; Support needs a playbook for that window.

I'm attaching an SLA exceptions summary that enumerates the quality delta for the fallback model and the proposed exception wording. If leadership is unwilling to accept the exception, we will need an operational budget to expand Dedicated pool capacity for Day 0.

Attachment: sla-exceptions-summary.xlsx (14 KB)

Grace — quick account note: Jordan Taylor (Acme) has confirmed the kickoff for July 6 and wants the option to scale to a custom pilot for two additional internal teams. Sales is aligned on a standard promotional credit for the first 30 days for named launch customers; finance approved a capped promo (see pricing slide in the QBR deck).

I reviewed Marcus's SLA exception request with Finance and Legal. They are open to an SLA exception for quality variance ONLY if we: 1) publish the fallback model behavior in the customer onboarding docs, 2) include a rollback and cache-warmup step in the runbook, and 3) get an explicit sign-off from Jordan for the pilot (I’ve asked Jordan to confirm via email, he is CC'd).

Also adding: Vivek, can you confirm that Support will accept the warm-up window procedure and have a standby engineer for the first 72 hours post-launch? We'll need a named pager owner.

—Laura
